correctness.rationale: A selected edge graph gives an acyclic rook line graph precisely when it is a linear forest. If both shores have degree-deficient vertices, maximality requires every opposite-shore deficient pair to lie in the same component; otherwise the joining edge could be added. Thus all deficient vertices are the two opposite-shore endpoints of one path, and every base vertex is in that path since any other component would have a deficient vertex. This forces a square. A saturated shore of size n≥m would give 2n≥m+n edges, impossible for a forest; in a square this rules out saturation of either shore. Thus a rectangular maximal edge set saturates the smaller shore, which suffices for maximality. Square paths have (m!)² undirected orderings. In a rectangle choose an ordered composition of m into s positive path sizes, order the m labels and choose an ordered list of m+s larger-shore labels, then divide by 2^s s! for orientations and path order. This independently gives every coefficient and its range, and agrees with the examples. Complementation and comparison of the degrees in m at fixed n−m prove the remaining claims.
residual_risks: The supplied finite enumeration was inspected, not replayed. The independently reconstructed classification and count establish the unrestricted result without those enumerations.

originality.rationale: Two earlier Resultary results jointly cover the claimed classification and entire component census. One explicitly identifies all maximal forests with the maximum forests and gives the same structural types; the other states the exact same maximum-forest component coefficients under identical labeled-board assumptions. The fixed-d limit follows by comparing degrees in that prior formula. The numerical consequences and refinements asserted here are thus already stated or immediate.
residual_risks: This is a statement-level demonstration of prior coverage, not a claim to identify the first publication of every scalar formula. In particular, the cited MathWorld passage alone does not establish the scalar priority attribution.
